body.query: What product did Kineto launch in August 2026?

documents.content:
JetBrains is offering early access to Kineto, an AI-powered, no-code development platform intended to help anybody create professional or personal apps regardless of technical ability\.

Launched August 5, Kineto helps users create, deploy, and maintain ready-to-use websites and small “single-value” apps without writing a single line of code, JetBrains said\. These apps could include a portfolio website, a family budget planner, or the next big app, the company noted\. Interested participants can join the waitlist at kineto\.dev\.

With Kineto, JetBrains said it was building a bridge between creative people, small businesses, and no-code platforms to open new era in which people will create their own personal web apps with minimal effort\. “The key principle behind Kineto is no code for you at all,” the blog post introducing Kineto said\. “We and our tools take care of the coding, so you could focus on being creative\. We’ve leveraged 25 years of experience building products for developers to create this technology that will help millions of people make their ideas happen—and truly enjoy the process of creation\.”

The initial step with Kineto is to formulate a prompt with a detailed explanation of what an app should do and what it should look like\. Each prompt is processed by Kineto and translated into the appropriate functionality\. Kineto asks users to choose a basic design template, font, and color scheme to provide a starting point for building an app\. Users then verify and modify functionality, user roles, and the rules of the app\. JetBrains said Kineto takes approximately 20 minutes to generate a prototype of a fully functional app\. Users then can add desired features, rehash the design, embed AI-generated illustrations or their own images, and publish the app\.

JetBrains, known for its Kotlin programming language, recently revealed it was also working on a high-abstraction language that would help make AI code generation more controllable, transparent, and useful\.

## Democratizing ⁤Development: JetBrains Launches kineto, a No-Code AI ‍App Builder

The landscape of software development is⁢ poised for a significant shift\. JetBrains, renowned for its ‍developer⁢ tools, has introduced‍ Kineto – an ⁢innovative, no-code submission builder powered by artificial intelligence\. this launch signals a move towards making app⁢ creation accessible to everyone,‍ nonetheless of coding expertise\.

Traditionally,⁢ building applications required extensive programming knowledge\. Now, kineto aims to ⁣change‌ that, envisioning a ⁤future where creating apps is as intuitive⁤ as⁢ typing, using spreadsheets, or editing videos​ on your ​smartphone\. ItS‍ a bold bet that app development can become a universally accessible ⁣skill, simply by​ *asking* for what ‌you need\.

### Kineto’s Early access Program:⁣ A Unique Opportunity

JetBrains isn’t simply releasing a beta product\.They’re actively ‍seeking creative individuals – even ⁢those with *zero* ⁢coding experience – to participate in an Early Access Programme\. This isn’t about clicking‍ through test cases; it’s about shaping the future of the platform\.If selected, you’ll receive dedicated support from the⁣ kineto team\. ⁢They will ⁤personally guide you through the process of bringing your app ideas to⁢ life\. This is a chance to be a pioneer, building something real with‍ a groundbreaking tool\.

### How Kineto Works: AI-Powered ⁤App Creation

Kineto leverages⁤ the power of AI to translate your ⁤ideas into ‌functional applications\. Rather of writing lines of code, you’ll describe what you want your app to do\. ‍The AI then handles the complexities ‌of development, generating ⁣the necessary code and interface elements\.​

Here’s what makes this approach notably compelling:

* **Accessibility:** No ⁣prior coding knowledge is required\.  
* **Speed:** Rapidly⁣ prototype and build applications\.  
* **Innovation:** Focus ⁤on your‌ idea, not the technical ⁢hurdles\.  
* **Support:** Direct assistance from the Kineto​ development team\.

### The Future of Software: ⁣Empowering Everyone

This ​launch represents a significant‍ step​ towards democratizing software development\. For years,the ability to create technology has been limited to a select few\. Kineto aims ⁤to break ⁣down those barriers,‌ empowering individuals and businesses to build custom solutions‌ tailored to their specific needs\.Consider the possibilities:

* **Entrepreneurs:** ​Quickly validate and launch your app ideas\.  
* **Small Businesses:** Create custom tools to ​streamline‌ operations\.  
* **Creatives:** Bring your unique visions to life without technical constraints\.* **Hobbyists:** Explore your ideas and build apps for personal use\.

### Staying Ahead⁣ of the Curve:⁤ AI ‍in Tech

The rise of AI is fundamentally changing the technology landscape\. Developers are increasingly ​recognizing the need to⁢ embrace these advancements or ‌risk falling behind\. The integration of ⁤AI into⁤ tools like Kineto isn’t‍ about⁤ replacing ‍developers;‌ it’s about augmenting‍ their​ capabilities and​ expanding ⁢the pool ​of potential creators\.

To delve deeper into⁣ the world of AI and‍ big data,⁤ consider attending industry events like the AI &⁤ Big Data⁣ Expo, taking place in​ Amsterdam, California, and london\. These events, alongside others like the Bright⁤ Automation Conference, BlockX, Digital Change Week, and the Cyber Security ‍& Cloud‌ Expo, offer invaluable​ insights from industry leaders\. You can explore a thorough calendar of enterprise technology events and webinars here\.

Kineto isn’t just a new tool;⁣ it’s a glimpse into the ⁣future⁣ of software development ⁤- a future where anyone can turn their ideas into reality\.

Cisco Systems and Kineto Wireless are working together to make it easier for mobile phone operators to move from trialing services that let mobile phone customers roam between Wi-Fi and cellular networks to offering commercial services, the companies planned to announce on Tuesday\.

The companies have linked Kineto’s controller, which lets mobile operators offer combined Wi-Fi and cellular services, with Cisco products that operators may already use, such as its authentication, authorization, and accounting server\.

Currently, Unlicensed Mobile Access \(UMA\), a specification used by Kineto and others that is designed to allow cellular operators to offer converged services, defines basic subscriber authentication\. “But it doesn’t provide for other information that an operator would want to have to turn this into a real service, like who can use the service, where they can use it and how they can pay,” said Steve Shaw, director of marketing for Kineto\.

Cisco and Kineto have linked their products so that Kineto’s controller can gather information such as subscription details about the user as well as identifying information about Wi-Fi access points and cellular networks in range of the user and pass that information to a Cisco authentication server used by the operator\. The Cisco server manages the service policy by validating the subscriber and the subscriber’s service plan and determining whether the service should be enabled over the nearby Wi-Fi access point\.

To date, operators are limited in how they authorize the service\. Operators that are trialing UMA services simply make the service fully available to the approved trailers, Shaw said\. In the case of British Telecommunications PLC \(BT\) and its Fusion service, BT ties users to just one access point \(AP\), located in their homes, he said\. “We’re now providing flexibility so if an operator wants to limit the service to one AP they can but if they want to enable service across a range of APs in an enterprise they can or they can tie service to a specific country,” he said\.

As part of the announcement on Tuesday, the companies also said that they’ve tested the interoperability between Kineto’s controller and Cisco’s Enhanced UMA Security Gateway, a product that aims to protect against threats from UMA devices to the mobile operator’s network\.

Shaw said that because this agreement with Cisco makes it easier for operators to deploy commercial offerings, end users are one step closer to being able to start using the services\. Enterprises are increasingly interested in such converged services because they can help reduce mobile phone costs by shifting mobile phone calls onto an enterprise Wi-Fi network, he said\.

In addition to UMA, other vendors are developing products based on SIP \(Session Initiation Protocol\) for delivering converged Wi-Fi and cellular services\. Some products could be deployed by an enterprise, rather than deployed and hosted by a cellular operator\.

# CyCognito introduces continuous AI pentesting to revolutionise cybersecurity assessments

CyCognito's new Continuous AI Pentesting aims to transform traditional, sporadic security testing into an ongoing, intelligent service, leveraging generative AI to better defend sprawling attack surfaces\.CyCognito has\.\.\.

CyCognito's new Continuous AI Pentesting aims to transform traditional, sporadic security testing into an ongoing, intelligent service, leveraging generative AI to better defend sprawling attack surfaces\.

CyCognito has launched Continuous AI Pentesting, folding AI-driven offensive testing into its exposure management platform in an attempt to move pentesting from occasional exercises to an ongoing service\. The company says the aim is to overcome the limits of traditional engagements, which are often too narrow, too expensive and too infrequent to keep pace with sprawling attack surfaces\.

Noah Intelligence surfaced the launch through continuous monitoring of public information, reflecting how specialist news can be read as a live signal on enterprise adoption, vendor direction and cyber exposure\.

The launch reflects a wider shift in the security market, where advances in generative AI have lowered the barrier for less skilled attackers\. CyCognito argues that defenders need to adopt similar capabilities if they want to identify weak points before they are exploited\. The company says its approach is designed to reach far beyond the small set of high-priority systems that usually receive manual attention\.

At the centre of the product is the Target Graph, a contextual layer that ties together the platform’s main components: Exposure Assessment, Exposure Validation and Threat Intelligence\. According to CyCognito, this structure helps the AI pentesting agents understand the organisation behind each asset, validate findings continuously and draw on vulnerability history, attacker playbooks and previous engagements to improve the quality of each test\. The company says new risk scenarios discovered by the agents can be turned into deterministic checks, allowing the system to learn over time and apply those lessons across customers\.

In announcing the feature, CyCognito also pointed to several examples uncovered through the work, including unauthorised access to a production CRM, a publicly readable retrieval-augmented generation index and building access systems exposed online\. The company says Continuous AI Pentesting is already running with selected design partners, including large enterprises and Fortune 500 groups\. Chief executive Rob Gurzeev said the project, internally called Project Kineto, is intended to make security testing behave less like a snapshot and more like a continuous stream of change-aware checks\.

Source: Noah Wire Services

# CyCognito launches continuous AI pentesting to counter increasing AI-driven threats

CyCognito introduces a pioneering continuous AI-powered pentesting platform designed to provide comprehensive, scalable, and adaptive security testing amid a rapidly evolving threat landscape shaped by AI tools, aiming\.\.\.

CyCognito introduces a pioneering continuous AI-powered pentesting platform designed to provide comprehensive, scalable, and adaptive security testing amid a rapidly evolving threat landscape shaped by AI tools, aiming to make offensive testing a constant process rather than a periodic task\.

CyCognito has unveiled Continuous AI Pentesting, a new capability that folds AI-driven offensive testing into its external exposure management platform and aims to make pentesting a permanent rather than occasional process\. In announcing the feature, the company said it is designed to overcome the coverage and cost limits of traditional engagements, which typically focus on a small set of high-priority assets\.

The move comes as security teams confront a shifting threat landscape shaped by more capable AI tools\. CyCognito argues that attackers no longer need large, highly skilled teams to launch effective campaigns, and that defenders must respond with similarly adaptive technology\. The company said its approach is built around a Target Graph, which ties together exposure assessment, continuous validation and threat intelligence so that the AI agents are working from richer asset context and exploitability evidence\. For insurers and risk engineers, Noah Intelligence would treat this kind of continuous offensive testing as a useful signal on technology risk, renewal conditions and the pace at which exposure can change\.

CyCognito says the system is intended to scale beyond the narrow slice of infrastructure usually covered by manual testing\. Its existing Continuous Validation capability already performs automated checks across external assets, and the new offering extends that model with agentic testing that can learn from each newly discovered risk\. According to the company, that makes the service self-improving over time, as fresh findings are converted into deterministic tests that can be reused across customers\.

The company has also highlighted the kinds of weaknesses the tool surfaced during development, including unauthorised access to production CRM data, an openly reachable retrieval-augmented knowledge base containing customer material and internal communications, and exposed building access systems connected to the public internet\. CyCognito said the project, internally known as Kineto, is already running with selected design partners, including large enterprises and Fortune 500 groups\.

The launch fits a broader industry debate over how far AI can go in offensive security\. Commentators at TechRadar have argued that AI is increasingly useful for accelerating testing and expanding coverage, but that human judgement still matters when it comes to interpreting business impact, prioritising risk and understanding attacker intent\. CyCognito’s pitch tries to bridge that divide by using AI to automate the repetitive parts of pentesting while retaining context-rich analysis in the platform itself\.

# AftermathFi's Perpetuals V2 launches on mainnet after 12-week security review clears all major issues

AftermathFi is bringing its Perpetuals V2 to mainnet on August 18, and for once, the security story behind a DeFi launch is actually worth reading\. Blockchain security firm OtterSec spent 12 weeks combing through nine separate repositories of the protocol’s smart contracts and came up empty on critical and high-severity issues, a result that matters considerably more given what happened the last time AftermathFi ran a perpetuals product in production\.

The Sui-based decentralized exchange announced the audit completion on August 14, leaving a narrow four-day window before the live launch\.

## What the audit actually covered

Twelve weeks is a long runway for a smart contract review\. OtterSec is not a new name in this space\. The firm has a track record of securing protocols with over $36B in total value locked and has patched vulnerabilities cumulatively exceeding $1B across its client base\. It had previously reviewed components of AftermathFi’s infrastructure, including the Perps Oracle, in late 2025, so the team was not coming in cold\.

## The shadow of the April exploit

On April 29, 2026, AftermathFi suffered an exploit that drained approximately $1\.14M USDC from its original Perpetuals module\. The mechanism was a negative integrator fee validation flaw, a bug that let attackers inflate collateral balances and then withdraw funds that were not legitimately theirs\. The team paused all operations and began an investigation\.

That incident is the direct reason Perpetuals V2 exists\. The protocol did not patch and resume; it rebuilt, subjected the new architecture to a substantially longer and broader audit than is typical, and is now launching with a clean bill of health from an established security firm\.

## What this means for AftermathFi and the Sui ecosystem

OtterSec’s continued involvement with AftermathFi infrastructure, stretching back to the Perps Oracle review in late 2025, adds a layer of institutional continuity to the security narrative\. The four days between the audit announcement and the mainnet date give the market very little time to react before the product is live\.

# GameStop’s Zelda Ocarina of Time Pre-Order “Leak” Looks Like an Error

Share this article

Nintendo has confirmed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time for Switch 2 in 2026, but it has not announced an official release date or pre-order schedule\. \(Nintendo\)

**Nintendo** officially announced **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** for **Switch 2** in June, but it has not yet revealed the game’s release date, price, or pre-order schedule\. That lack of information recently turned what appears to be a retailer error into a widely shared Zelda “leak\.”

A GameStop search result reportedly displayed an August 4, 2026 date alongside the upcoming Ocarina of Time release\. Some fans interpreted the date as the start of pre-orders or even a possible launch date\.

However, the available evidence suggests that the date probably did not belong to Zelda at all\.

## The August 4 Date Likely Came From Another Game

August 4, 2026 is the confirmed release date for Beast of Reincarnation, an upcoming action RPG from Game Freak\. GameStop already has active product pages and pre-order information for the game\.

This makes a retailer database or search indexing error the most plausible explanation\. GameStop or Google may have pulled the August 4 date from Beast of Reincarnation and temporarily attached it to the Ocarina of Time search result\.

GameStop subsequently removed the date, and Nintendo has not made any related announcement\.

The incident therefore should not be treated as confirmation that Ocarina of Time pre-orders will begin on August 4\. It also does not reliably indicate when Nintendo will hold its next presentation\.

Retailer listings sometimes reveal games, editions, or release dates before publishers announce them\. However, they can also contain placeholders, copied product data, and incorrectly matched information\. In this case, the connection to another confirmed August 4 release makes the error explanation particularly convincing\.

**Newly released game**: Palworld 1\.0 Patch Notes: 72 New Pals, World Tree, Sunreach and Major Changes

## Nintendo Has Only Confirmed a 2026 Release

Nintendo officially revealed The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time during its June 9 Nintendo Direct\. The company said the Nintendo 64 classic would return for a new generation exclusively on Switch 2 in 2026\.

The brief announcement trailer introduced the project but did not show extended gameplay\. Nintendo also withheld the exact release date, price, editions, and pre-order details\.

The company’s official store page still lists only “Coming 2026\.” It does not currently offer a purchase or pre-order button\.

Nintendo has also avoided explaining the full scope of the project\. The announcement describes Ocarina of Time as “reborn,” but we still do not know how closely it will follow the original game or the enhanced Nintendo 3DS version\.

More information should arrive before launch, particularly details about its updated visuals, controls, gameplay revisions, and technical performance on Switch 2\.

**See also**: Bethesda Finally Reveals What Comes Next for Fallout and The Elder Scrolls VI

## Play-Asia Lists the Game for $59\.99

Although GameStop does not currently accept Ocarina of Time pre-orders, Play-Asia has published product pages for several regional physical editions\.

The retailer lists the game for $59\.99 and marks its expected shipping date as TBA\. Customers can currently add the product to their carts, but Nintendo has not confirmed the price\.

The $59\.99 figure could represent genuine distributor information\. It could also be an estimated or placeholder price that Play-Asia will update later\.

Buyers should therefore avoid treating it as Nintendo’s official US launch price\. Nintendo could use different pricing across physical and digital editions, regions, or special packages\.

The listing does at least support the expectation that Ocarina of Time will receive a physical Switch 2 release\. However, final availability, packaging, and regional language support could change before launch\.

**Related news**: Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake Listed at $59\.99 Ahead of Nintendo Price Confirmation

## When Will Official Pre-Orders Begin?

Nintendo has not announced when pre-orders will open\. Any specific date remains speculation until Nintendo or an authorized retailer publishes confirmed purchase information\.

A new Nintendo Direct or dedicated Zelda presentation would be the most likely place for the company to reveal gameplay, editions, pricing, and a firm release date\. Retail pre-orders could open shortly after that announcement\.

For now, fans should treat the August 4 GameStop date as an apparent listing error rather than a reliable leak\.

The remake itself is official, and Nintendo still plans to release it for Switch 2 in 2026\. The rumored pre-order date is not\.

# Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026: All the latest news, price and launch updates

The Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026 is officially on the way, with the retailer becoming one of the latest to confirm its festive countdown and open waitlist sign-ups ahead of launch\. It joins Harrods, Cult Beauty and Sephora among the best beauty advent calendars announced so far, with retailers revealing their offerings earlier than they did in 2025, when launches largely began at the end of August and start of September\.

While Space NK is keeping most details under wraps for now, its brand manager Abbey Parkinson has teased “iconic hero products \[and\] exciting discovery brands,” giving beauty obsessives plenty to look forward to when the contents are unveiled later this month\. Particularly given the highly-coveted roster of products Space NK’s previous calendars \(think: K18, Refy and Westman Atelier\) have carried\.

I'll be updating this guide as more information is announced, including the contents list \(coming 19 August\), the official on-sale date and everything else you’ll need to know before it goes live\. Scroll on for all the early details, from pricing to packaging\.

**Read more: ****Everything we know so far about Cult Beauty’s 2026 advent calendar**

### Space NK beauty advent calendar 2026

At £275, the Space NK beauty advent calendar is £15 more expensive than last year's edition, but the retailer says its contents will be worth more than £1,200 \(£50 extra than 2025’s\), which still leaves you with an extra £35 of savings up for grabs\. With the full line-up still hush hush until 19 August, it's too early to say whether this price and worth increase will definitely result in a higher value product\. But I’m expecting more premium brands, additional full-size products and perhaps some bigger-ticket beauty buys\.

So far, Space NK has only teased a mix of \"iconic hero products\" and \"exciting discovery brands\.\" Looking at its recent brand onboardings, it’d be great to see the likes of Prequel and Takami featuring alongside established beauty favourites – and in-keeping with Parkinson’s ‘discovery brand’ suggestion\.

The calendar itself has been given a festive makeover, with pastel pink and blue nutcracker-splashed packaging that's – according to Space NK – also more environmentally conscious\. It's made from 100 per cent recyclable FSC-certified paper, printed using vegetable-based inks and designed to be reused or recycled after Christmas\.

Whether you’re waiting for the full list of contents or dead set on securing the Space NK advent this December, you’ll want to join the waitlist sooner rather than later\. Rather than giving everyone access at once, Space NK has declared that “the sooner you join, the earlier you can shop on preview day,” which implies that links to the live calendar will be sent based on when signees joined the waitlist\. So, an earlier place in the queue could improve your chances of getting hold of one before it sells out\. And, in my experience, it definitely will sell out\.

#### What to know

- **Price:** £275 \(up £15 year on year\)
- **Worth:** £1,200\+ \(up £50 year on year\)
- **Number of days:** 25
- **Number of products:** Not yet revealed
- **Advent calendar highlights:** Products announced 7am, 19 August – \"iconic hero products with exciting discovery brands\" promised
- **Available:** Not yet announced, waitlist open now
